rationale.selected_because: The operational objective is to establish whether the window work has actually resolved the reported fault and then decide whether completion is appropriate. The latest tenant email reports “All jobs was done,” but the earlier tenant report said parts needed ordering, and the tenant says contractor Richard promised a report. Request that report, acknowledge the tenant’s update, inform the landlord, and put the case into completion review without treating work as verified or closing it.

assumptions: The tenant’s September 10 reference to all jobs and Richard’s promised report concerns the ongoing window work, given the September 2 parts-order update and the continuity of the tenant’s account. No unrelated extracted work-order ID is used as evidence for actions on this request.
alternatives_considered: Closing the request based on the tenant’s broad statement was not selected because the earlier parts-order report leaves the repair outcome materially unclear.

A new appointment or another request to the tenant to confirm completion was not selected: the tenant has already reported completion, and the outstanding useful evidence is the contractor’s promised report.

actions.value: Review the reported completion; do not treat the repair as verified or close the request yet.

actions.message: The tenant now reports that all jobs were done. Their earlier update said parts needed ordering, and they report that Richard promised a report. We are requesting the contractor’s attendance and repair details and will review completion when that response is available.
